The test image shows soybean seeds — one normal tan seed (upper left), one with dark, crusty/moldy fungal growth covering most of the seed surface, concentrated around the hilum area. This is a seed-level symptom.

Top candidates: **Purple_Seed_Stain** (pink/purple from hilum), **Phomopsis** (cracked, shriveled, white mold), **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus** (hilum pigment diffusion/mottling), **Downy_mildew** (dull white crusty fungal mass on seeds).

Let me view reference images for my top candidates.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Shows two soybean seeds — one healthy tan seed (upper left) and one with very dark (near-black), crusty/textured discoloration covering most of the seed surface, concentrated around the hilum area.

- **Purple_Seed_Stain reference**: Shows seeds with varying degrees of pink-to-dark-purple/black staining extending from the hilum, including some severely affected seeds that appear almost entirely dark — matches the test image well.

- **Phomopsis reference**: Shows pods with dark lesions; seed symptoms described as chalky **white** mold — doesn't match the dark appearance.

- **Downy_mildew reference**: Shows leaf symptoms; seed symptoms described as dull **white** crusty mass — doesn't match the dark coloration.

The test image seed shows the characteristic hallmark of **Purple_Seed_Stain**: dark pigmentation (from Cercospora kikuchii) extending from the hilum across the seed coat with a rough, discolored surface, contrasting with a normal tan/beige seed alongside it.
